summary: This component creates an interactive project scaffolding tool that lets users view, copy, and download a file structure. It accepts either child components (like snippets and guidelines) or a flat file map, then renders them as expandable code blocks, generates a bash script to recreate the folder structure, and provides a ZIP download button.

explanations.22: This creates a marker component — it's just a placeholder that doesn't render anything, but the `isGuideline` property attached to it lets other code identify it later.
explanations.28: Similar to Guideline, this creates an empty placeholder component with an `isEmptyFolder` marker property so the parent can recognize it.
explanations.47:
This function walks through nested React elements and extracts just the plain text, stripping away any wrapper elements like `

` tags that MDX might add.
explanations.95: This caches the parsed file list, guidelines, and folder names so they're only recalculated when the input `files` or `children` change, not on every button click.
explanations.113: Since React's type system doesn't know about our custom `isGuideline` property, we cast the child's type to an object with optional properties we're checking for.
explanations.130: This checks if the element is actually a file component by looking for either the Snippet component, a filename/title prop, or checking that it's not a plain HTML element.
explanations.155: This generates and caches the bash one-liner script, recalculating only when the file list or folder structure changes, not when UI toggles change.
explanations.167: This uses a bash heredoc (the `<<'DELIMITER'` syntax) to safely write file content that might contain special characters without needing escaping.
explanations.182: This copies the script to the clipboard and temporarily shows a "Copied!" message for 2 seconds, using a ref to track the timeout so it can be cleaned up if the component unmounts.
explanations.189: This async function creates a ZIP file by adding all folders and files to it, then optionally includes a README with the guidelines, and finally triggers a download in the browser.
explanations.199: This removes any leading slashes from the folder name to prevent invalid zip paths like `/tmp/project`, which would create problems when extracting.
explanations.327: If the original component (like a Snippet) was passed in, this clones it and updates its props with the parsed content and the expandAll state, preserving any original styling or behavior.
explanations.340: If no original component exists (files came from the flat `files` map), this renders a generic Snippet component with the filename and content.
